documents.title: Establishing Expectations: Syllabus Language and Policies for Generative AI Use
documents.summary: Faculty-center page telling instructors to set AI expectations in each syllabus. It offers four use levels and three sample syllabus statements (allow, prohibit, require), stating these are not official MSU policy.
documents.stance_why: The page sets no rule itself: it says the examples 'are not official MSU policies' and offers four levels ('It's not allowed', 'allowed with appropriate attribution', 'allowed in limited instances', 'encouraged broadly or required') for each instructor to choose, so the stance is delegates with tiers.

units.why: The CFE tells instructors to 'set expectations for students in the syllabus', which is a requirement to state AI expectations; P09 fits better than P04 because it is about communicating, not about who decides.
units.anchor: Instructors should set expectations for students in the syllabus, discussions in class
units.frag_start: Instructors should set expectations for students
units.frag_end: can be used from the beginning.

units.why: The list of 'Four examples' sorts AI use into named levels (not allowed, attribution, limited, encouraged or required), so it is a tier scheme (P05).
units.anchor: Four examples for content-generating AI could be:
units.frag_start: Four examples for content-generating AI

units.why: First tier: 'It's not allowed: Only content done by a student ... is accepted', a default ban option for an assignment (P01).
units.anchor: Only content done by a student or as part of an assigned group is accepted.
units.frag_start: It's not allowed: Only content

units.why: Second tier allows AI-assisted work if 'students clearly identify what parts of the assignment were AI generated'; the disclosure condition is the core, so P24 rather than P02.
units.anchor: students clearly identify what parts of the assignment were AI generated
units.frag_start: It's allowed with appropriate attribution

units.why: Third tier: AI 'can be used to prepare for assignments by brainstorming, but students must show how it helped'; brainstorming-only use is P15.
units.anchor: AI can be used to prepare for assignments by brainstorming
units.frag_start: It's allowed in limited instances

units.why: Fourth tier: 'Use is encouraged broadly or required', an option where AI is welcomed or expected (P02).
units.anchor: Use is encouraged broadly or required: Students can use AI but must identify
units.frag_start: Use is encouraged broadly or required

units.why: The page says the examples 'are not official MSU policies' and only help faculty write policies 'for their individual courses', so the decision stays with each instructor (P04).
units.anchor: these are not official MSU policies around generative AI use
units.frag_start: Please note these are not official

units.why: Example 'allowing' language says 'you may utilize AI language models, including ChatGPT, as a resource to support your writing assignments'; it is about prose, so P18.

units.frag_start: If you choose to use this tool, apply it

units.frag_start: I encourage you to use AI

documents.unit: Montana University System, Commissioner of Higher Education
documents.title: Commissioner's Directive: Generative AI Adoption and Use
documents.summary: System directive from the Commissioner of Higher Education telling campuses to engage with eight AI principles and adopt essential practices for procurement, instruction and research. It sets no student-use rule and leaves instruction expectations to campuses.
documents.stance_why: The directive directs campuses to adopt practices 'as appropriate to institutional context' and to establish 'clear AI use expectations for instruction' but sets no AI-use rule for students, so it hands decisions to campuses and instructors (delegates).

units.why: The directive says it 'establishes a shared framework for responsible AI use across the Montana University System' with principles and practices, an institution-level framework (P56).
units.anchor: establishes a shared framework for responsible AI use across the Montana University System
units.frag_start: That document establishes a shared framework

units.why: The preamble names risks 'to data privacy and security, academic integrity, research reliability, and equity of access', framing purpose; chosen P56 since it lists several concerns rather than one rule.
units.anchor: threats to data privacy and security, academic integrity, research reliability, and equity of access
units.frag_start: They also introduce real risks

units.why: Campuses 'are directed to' review and discuss 'the eight core principles', an obligation to engage with the system framework (P56).
units.anchor: review and discuss the eight core principles
units.frag_start: Campus CEOs and chief academic officers should ensure
units.frag_end: use of approved and non-approved tools.
units.policy: Campus CEOs and chief academic officers ensure that leadership, faculty governance bodies and administrative units review and discuss the eight MUS core principles for AI use.

units.why: 'Each MUS institution shall review ... and adopt those practices in institutional policy' is a mandate to adopt campus-level practices (P56).
units.anchor: Each MUS institution shall review the campus essential practices
units.frag_start: Each MUS institution shall review

units.why: Campuses 'are expected to give particular attention to establishing clear AI use expectations for instruction'; this asks for instruction expectations to be set (P09).
units.anchor: establishing clear AI use expectations for instruction

units.anchor: risk-based procurement safeguards

units.why: Campuses should attend to 'reinforcing research integrity standards for AI-assisted scholarship', i.e. AI in research (P62).

units.why: OCHE will develop 'system-wide AI literacy resources for students, faculty, and staff' and professional development; supports learning AI (P63).

units.frag_start: working with state and MUS procurement
